```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Multi-Omics Integration using mixOmics DIABLO (Multiblock sPLS-DA)
# ==============================================================================

#BiocManager::install("mixOmics")
# Load mixOmics library
library(mixOmics)

set.seed(123) # For reproducibility
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data Preparation
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
data(breast.TCGA)

# Extract predictor blocks (X) and sample outcome labels (Y)
X <- list(
  mRNA    = breast.TCGA$data.train$mrna,
  miRNA   = breast.TCGA$data.train$mirna,
  protein = breast.TCGA$data.train$protein
)

Y <- breast.TCGA$data.train$subtype  # Categorical class labels (e.g., Basal, Her2, LumA)

# Define design matrix (connection between datasets: 0.1 for trade-off between discrimination and correlation)
design <- matrix(0.1, ncol = length(X), nrow = length(X), 
                 dimnames = list(names(X), names(X)))
diag(design) <- 0
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Parameter Tuning (Components & Feature Selection)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Step 2a: Estimate performance to choose optimal number of components
diablo.unsparse <- block.plsda(X, Y, ncomp = 5, design = design)
perf.diablo <- perf(diablo.unsparse, validation = 'Mfold', folds = 5, nrepeat = 10)

# Extract recommended number of components (using BER / Centroids distance)
ncomp <- perf.diablo$choice.ncomp$WeightedVote["Overall.BER", "centroids.dist"]
if (is.na(ncomp) || ncomp < 2) ncomp <- 2  # Default to at least 2 components for plotting
```

```{r}
# Step 2b: Fine-tune the number of features to select from each omics block (keepX)
test.keepX <- list(
  mRNA    = c(5:10, 15, 20),
  miRNA   = c(5:10, 15, 20),
  protein = c(5:10, 15, 20)
)

tune.diablo <- tune.block.splsda(
  X, Y, 
  ncomp = ncomp, 
  test.keepX = test.keepX, 
  design = design, 
  validation = 'Mfold', 
  folds = 5, 
  nrepeat = 5
)

list.keepX <- tune.diablo$choice.keepX
list.keepX
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Fit Final DIABLO Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
final.diablo <- block.splsda(
  X = X, 
  Y = Y, 
  ncomp = ncomp, 
  keepX = list.keepX, 
  design = design
)

print("Final selected features per block and component:")
print(final.diablo$keepX)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Diagnostic & Integration Visualizations
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Plot 1: Diagnostic Correlation Plot ---
# Verifies correlation between latent components across data blocks
plotDiablo(final.diablo, ncomp = 1)
```

```{r}
# --- Plot 2: Sample Projections Across Blocks ---
# Displays sample clustering in latent space for each individual omics block
plotIndiv(
  final.diablo, 
  ind.names = FALSE, 
  legend = TRUE, 
  title = "DIABLO Sample Subtype Separation"
)
```

```{r}
# --- Plot 3: Feature Loadings ---
# Highlights top signature variables driving classification per block
plotLoadings(final.diablo, comp = 1, contrib = 'max', method = 'median')
```

```{r}
# --- Plot 4: Circos Plot ---
# Shows cross-omics feature correlations (|r| > 0.7) connecting key biomarkers
circosPlot(
  final.diablo, 
  cutoff = 0.7, 
  line = TRUE, 
  color.blocks = c("darkorchid", "brown1", "lightseagreen"),
  color.cor = c("chocolate1", "skyblue")
)
```

```{r}
# --- Plot 5: Clustered Image Map (Heatmap) ---
# Multi-block correlation heatmap of top selected features
pdf("diablo_heatmap.pdf", width = 12, height = 12)
cimDiablo(final.diablo, margins = c(8, 12), color.Y = c("purple", "orange", "cyan"))
dev.off()
```
